method: Three fresh reviewers each, given only the nine blind sheets (docs/jclass-11/blind/<surface>.jpg) and the cards' level descriptions, put each sheet's letters A to E in level order (each level once) and named the least convincing thing on each sheet. Rule (wear_check.py): a reviewer passes a surface with all five right or one swap of neighbouring levels; a surface passes when at least three reviewers do.

least_real.paint: L4 barnacle crust is an even grey speckle over the whole bottom, and the rust runs are evenly spaced vertical stripes
least_real.teak: L3 is beige, not almost white-blond, and hard to tell from L1
least_real.varnish: L4 cabin peeling is a regular brick-like patchwork of orange flakes on grey
least_real.bronze: the L3 bronze shows no black patina in the recesses and looks almost the same as L1
least_real.duralumin: L4 flaking is an even dark speckle over the whole mast, not clusters round the fittings, and there is no white corrosion powder
least_real.cotton: L4 grime is soft vertical brown banding; the mildew doesn't follow the folds and no rust streaks from the hanks show
least_real.manila: L0 to L3 rope barely changes (no visible hairiness); the levels read mostly from the deck
least_real.wire: the wire itself is too small to read; the levels come from the deck and hull, not the wire
least_real.furnishings: the L4 deckhead is a rough noisy texture, and the L1 to L3 velvet and carpet differences are very faint

least_real.paint: L4 rust runs are evenly spaced vertical stripes like a barcode, and the barnacled bottom reads as flat grey noise. The kept L3 hull has faded, streaky antifouling much like L2's
least_real.teak: the levels differ mostly by an overall colour shift. L4's green algae, black mildew and proud failed seams hardly show
least_real.varnish: the peeled deckhouse varnish at L4 is a blocky, brick-like patchwork of orange tiles on grey, not flakes along the grain
least_real.bronze: the L4 winch base flakes to bright silver-white, as if paint were coming off metal, and the verdigris lies as an even all-over coat
least_real.duralumin: the L4 corrosion is evenly scattered dark specks over the whole mast, not flaking clustered round the fittings with white powder
least_real.cotton: the L4 mildew is a uniform grey wash with speckle, not spotting along the folds. No rust streaks from the hanks are visible
least_real.manila: the rope itself barely changes from L0 to L3, so the deck and bronze carry the ladder. The L4 fraying and fuzz don't read
least_real.wire: the wire is hardly visible in the crop: the levels read from the deck, the hull and the green, verdigris-looking turnbuckles rather than from rusting galvanised wire
least_real.furnishings: L0 to L3 are nearly identical (only the saturation shifts slightly). At L4 the blue velvet turns uniformly grey and the ceiling turns into coarse mottled noise

least_real.varnish: L4 peel on the cabin trunk reads as blotchy brick-like patches, not flakes along the grain
least_real.bronze: L4 winch is an even green-brown camouflage mottle; L2/L3 hand-polish vs dark recesses hardly shows
least_real.duralumin: mast wear is evenly scattered dark speckle over the whole spar, not flake clusters round the fittings
least_real.cotton: mildew is uniform speckle across the furled sail rather than along the folds; hank rust streaks hard to read

least_real.furnishings: L4 stains are big uniform smudges over walls, ceiling and carpet, like a dirt overlay; L0-L3 nearly identical
